newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp-Risks involved in any German rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp-Risks involved in any German rate cut.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Thursday that a Bundesbank interest rate cut at the present would entail "considerable risks".

Krupp told a news conference that it could not be ruled out that a rate cut would affect exchange rates and thereby possibly boost import prices and unemployment. It might also lead to an increase in bond yields, he said.

Krupp also noted that interest rate differentials in Europe had narrowed considerably. "Therefore interest rate cuts at the moment would entail considerable risks. One would have to keep checking whether the expected advantages are sufficiently great to warrant taking the risks," he said.

Krupp also said those speculating that the Bundesbank may have to raise interest rates in the light of an apparent change in trend to higher U.S. rates should take into account that the economic situation in the U.S. was completely different from the German position.
Krupp was speaking at the annual conference of the state central bank of Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, and Schleswig-Holstein, of which he is president.
